name: HTML
summary: The markup language of the World Wide Web. Since 2019 the WHATWG HTML Living Standard is the single authoritative definition; it specifies the element vocabulary and content models, the DOM-based data model, and an exact error-tolerant parsing algorithm (tokenizer state machine plus tree-construction insertion modes).

level_notes.0: HTML is defined by a specification, not an implementation, but the parsing chapter is an executable algorithm, so parsers are near-transliterations of it. Listed: html5lib (the first implementation, with the shared html5lib-tests corpus), web-platform-tests (the conformance suite), html5ever, parse5, the Gecko/Blink/WebKit/Ladybird parsers, several library parsers, the Nu Html Checker (RELAX NG schemas for document conformance) and the spec source itself. The html5lib-tests tree-construction files are linked as a directory because raw file fetches of that path fail from the research sandbox.
level_notes.1: The WHATWG HTML Living Standard is normative (W3C ceased publishing a competing HTML in 2019; see the MOU). Section numbers in titles drift as the standard changes; the fragment ids are stable. Historical versions (the 1992 "HTML Tags" note, RFC 1866, HTML 3.2, HTML 4.01, W3C HTML5) are included for history. w3.org answers some automated clients with 403, so those links may show as blocked in the link checker; they were verified manually.
level_notes.2: MDN and web.dev are the main maintained tutorials/references; Simon Pieters' "Idiosyncrasies of the HTML parser" is the standard secondary text on the syntax and parser.
